"Don't cross the Lakshman Rekha." Everyone knows the line. Valmiki's Ramayana never draws it.
Myth vs Text · 3

What the texts say:
• Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 45: Sita, terrified for Rama, sends Lakshmana after him. Before leaving, he draws no line. He asks the forest deities to protect her (45.33–34) and goes, looking back again and again.
• Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas (16th century), Lanka Kanda: Mandodari taunts Ravana: "Rama's younger brother drew a small line, and you couldn't even cross that."
• Later retellings, and the screen, made the line famous.

Retellings are a living layer of the tradition. Here we just show what the oldest text says.

Which Ramayana did you grow up with: Valmiki, Tulsidas, a regional one, or the TV serial? Tell us 👇

You know him as Karna. It was not the name he was born with.
Part 11 of the Mahabharata, from the very beginning.

A young princess, Pritha (Kunti), daughter of Sura and aunt of Krishna, served the fearsome sage Durvasa. Pleased, he gave her a mantra: any god she summoned would give her a son. Curious, she tested it on the Sun. Surya appeared; she begged his pardon, but a god's coming "cannot be futile". A son was born at once, "accoutred with natural armour and with face brightened by ear-rings". Afraid of her family, she cast him into the water. A charioteer and his wife Radha raised him as Vasusena. Years later he cut off his armour and gave it to Indra, who came disguised as a Brahmin, and so he was called Karna. Told from the Adi Parva (Ganguli translation, section CXI).

"Baby Hanuman swallowed the sun." Everyone knows the story. Valmiki's Ramayana never says it.
Myth vs Text · 4

What the texts say:
• Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 66.21–24: the child sees the rising sun, thinks it is a fruit, and leaps into the sky to seize it. Indra hurls his thunderbolt; it strikes his jaw (hanu), "hence your name, Hanuman". (The Uttara Kanda retelling, 35–36, has him seize the sun and meet Rahu, but still no swallowing.)
• Hanuman Chalisa, chaupai 18: "जुग सहस्र जोजन पर भानू। लील्यो ताहि मधुर फल जानू॥" (he swallowed the sun, thousands of yojanas away, thinking it a sweet fruit).

Both stories are loved and part of the living tradition. Here we just show what Valmiki says.

Five Pandava brothers. Not one of them was Pandu's own son.
Part 12 of the Mahabharata, from the very beginning.

Hunting on the slopes of the Himalayas, King Pandu shot a great deer and its mate. But the deer cried out in a human voice: it was the sage Kindama in disguise. Dying, he cursed Pandu: the day he embraced his wife, he would die. Pandu gave away his jewels and became a forest hermit with his wives, Kunti and Madri. Without sons his line would end, so Kunti told him her secret, the mantra of the sage Durvasa. She called Dharma, and Yudhishthira was born; Vayu, the wind, and Bhima was born; Indra, and Arjuna was born. Then Madri called the twin Ashvins and bore Nakula and Sahadeva. Five sons of the gods. But the curse was waiting. Told from the Adi Parva (Ganguli translation, sections CXVIII–CXXIV).

यमराज उसके पति को ले गए। वो उन्हें वापस ले आई। 🔥
महाभारत की एक कहानी: सावित्री और सत्यवान

नारद मुनि ने चेतावनी दी थी कि सत्यवान एक साल में मर जाएगा, फिर भी सावित्री ने उसी से विवाह किया। ठीक एक साल बाद, जंगल में यमराज आए और सत्यवान के प्राण ले चले। सावित्री उनके पीछे चल दी। प्रसन्न होकर यमराज ने वरदान दिए, बस पति के प्राण छोड़कर: ससुर की आँखें, उनका राज्य, पिता के लिए सौ पुत्र, और सत्यवान से सौ पुत्र। "तथास्तु।" तब सावित्री ने पूछा: पति के बिना ये वरदान सच कैसे होगा? और यमराज ने फंदा खोल दिया।
(महाभारत, वन पर्व, पतिव्रता-माहात्म्य पर्व)

अँधेरी रात। एक तीर। और एक श्राप, जिसने राजा दशरथ की जान ली। 💔
रामायण की एक कहानी: श्रवण कुमार

युवा दशरथ सिर्फ़ आवाज़ सुनकर निशाना लगा सकते थे। एक बरसाती रात, सरयू किनारे पानी भरने की आवाज़ को उन्होंने हाथी समझा और तीर चला दिया। वो एक युवा तपस्वी था, जो अपने अंधे माता-पिता के लिए पानी लेने आया था। सच जानकर पिता ने श्राप दिया: "जैसे मैं पुत्र के लिए तड़प रहा हूँ, वैसे ही तुम भी पुत्र-शोक में मरोगे।" सालों बाद, राम के वन जाने पर, यही हुआ।
(वाल्मीकि रामायण, अयोध्या कांड, सर्ग 63–64। वाल्मीकि उस तपस्वी का नाम नहीं लेते; "श्रवण कुमार" नाम बाद की कथाओं से प्रसिद्ध हुआ।)

देवताओं का सबसे बड़ा हथियार, एक ऋषि की हड्डियों से बना था। ⚡
महाभारत की एक कहानी: महर्षि दधीचि

असुर वृत्र और कालकेयों से हारकर देवता ब्रह्मा जी के पास पहुँचे। ब्रह्मा जी ने कहा: ऋषि दधीचि के पास जाओ, और तीनों लोकों के भले के लिए उनकी हड्डियाँ माँगो। दधीचि मुस्कुराए: "जिसमें तुम्हारा भला है, वही होगा। मैं ये शरीर स्वयं त्याग दूँगा।" और उसी पल प्राण त्याग दिए। उनकी हड्डियों से त्वष्टा ने वज्र बनाया, और उसी वज्र से इंद्र ने वृत्र का वध किया।
(महाभारत, वन पर्व, तीर्थयात्रा पर्व, अध्याय 100–101)
